Calculate time-based sample weights for MAP Bayesian fitting

Source: R/calculate_fit_weights.R
calculate_fit_weights.Rd

Computes the weights a weighting scheme assigns to a set of observation times. This is the calculation run_eval() applies internally at each iteration when a scheme is passed to its weights argument, and is exported so the effect of a scheme and its parameters can be previewed before running an evaluation. To use a scheme in run_eval(), pass a fit_weights() object, not the output of this function.

Usage

calculate_fit_weights(weights = NULL, t = NULL)

Arguments

weights

weighting scheme: a fit_weights() object, a string with the scheme name, or a named list with a scheme element plus optional scheme-specific parameters.

t

numeric vector of observation times (in hours)

Value

numeric vector of weights the same length as t, or NULL if weights is NULL or the scheme is not recognized.

Details

weights may be a fit_weights() object, a string naming a scheme, or a named list with a scheme element plus optional scheme-specific parameters (e.g. list(scheme = "weight_gradient_exponential", t12_decay = 72)). See fit_weights() for the available schemes and their parameters.

Examples

t <- c(0, 24, 48, 96)
calculate_fit_weights(fit_weights("weight_last_two_only"), t = t)
#> [1] 0 0 1 1
calculate_fit_weights(
  fit_weights("weight_gradient_exponential", t12_decay = 72),
  t = t
)
#> [1] 0.3968503 0.5000000 0.6299605 1.0000000
